b: Vague promises provide cover for the uncommitted.
Commitment restricts options and expands freedom.
The Paradox of Commitment is Freedom
The things you refuse to pursue determine what you can accomplish.
Freedom from indecision. Eliminate the exhausting need to keep choosing.
Freedom from distraction. Say no to attractive distractions. Give your best energy to what matters most.
Freedom from convenience. Do hard things when less meaningful options are available.
Freedom to develop mastery. Stay engaged long enough to move beyond superficial competence.
Freedom to build trust. Keep your promises. Dependability earns trust.
Freedom from fleeting emotions. Follow your values instead of your mood.
Freedom to find meaning. Commitment transforms ordinary effort into purposeful contribution.
Begin with: “Let’s be sure you’re clear.”
What will it look like when you succeed?
Who depends on you to get this done?
What obstacles make this a challenge? How will you address them?
What resources or support do you need?
After commitment, the only question is, “How will this get done?” Distill responsibility into action items.
A person who signs on has the will. Help them find a way.
Healthy commitment is devotion to a worthy purpose, not blind loyalty to a failing plan.
Commit to the destination. Stay flexible about the path.
What possibilities must die for you to enjoy the paradox of commitment?
